text: The latest update did not improve battery life at all.
rationale: Tests whether the model picks up the negation cue or just the trigger word 'improve'.

text: I fail to see how this is considered an upgrade.
rationale: Uses 'fail' and 'considered' to test subtle negation of the positive word 'upgrade'.

text: This app is nothing like the perfect tool it used to be.
rationale: Tests if the model ignores the negation 'nothing like' and over-indexes on 'perfect'.

text: Not exactly the masterpiece they promised us.
rationale: Tests ironic negation 'Not exactly' combined with a highly positive word 'masterpiece'.

text: This app is no longer reliable on my phone.
rationale: Strong positive cue 'reliable' negated by 'no longer'; tests cue-vs-context handling.

text: The customer service was surprisingly terrible.
rationale: Pairs a positive adverb 'surprisingly' with a negative adjective to confuse simple bag-of-words.

text: I finally managed to uninstall this completely.
rationale: The word 'uninstall' is usually negative in reviews but here the user achieved their goal ('managed to').

text: An absolute disaster from start to finish.
rationale: Uses 'absolute' (often used positively like 'absolute best') to modify a negative word.

text: The team won the championship final last weekend.
rationale: Sports content unrelated to app-review training; tests domain-shift robustness.

text: Add two cups of flour and bake for 30 minutes.
rationale: Recipe instructions should be neutral but contain action verbs that might trigger false confidence.

text: The new superhero movie broke box office records.
rationale: Entertainment news with strong verbs ('broke records'); testing if it predicts positive instead of neutral.

text: The prime minister announced a new economic plan.
rationale: Political news; testing if formal language defaults to a specific sentiment.

text: Ok.
rationale: Extremely short text; tests if lack of features defaults to neutral or random.

text: Wow!
rationale: Single exclamation word; tests if punctuation is enough for a positive classification.

text: No.
rationale: Single negative word; tests baseline handling of minimal negative input.

text: I installed the app yesterday morning while I was eating breakfast and watching the news on television. The weather was a bit cloudy, but I decided to sit near the window anyway. After finishing my coffee, I opened the app, scrolled through the menus for about twenty minutes without doing anything specific, and then closed it to go for a walk.
rationale: Extremely long, descriptive text with no sentiment; tests if length alone confuses the model.

text: Oh great, another update that deletes all my saved files. Thanks!
rationale: Uses explicitly positive words ('great', 'Thanks') in a highly negative sarcastic context.

text: I just love it when the app crashes right before I save.
rationale: Uses 'love' in a sarcastic manner regarding a severe bug ('crashes').

text: What a brilliant idea to hide the logout button in a maze.
rationale: Uses 'brilliant' sarcastically to describe bad UI design.

text: 10/10 for finding new ways to completely ruin my day.
rationale: Uses a positive rating format '10/10' paired with negative outcome 'ruin my day'.

text: I can't recommend this highly enough.
rationale: Double negation structure ('can't' + 'highly enough') which actually means extreme praise.

text: This solved the horrible bug that was destroying my workflow.
rationale: Contains mostly negative words ('horrible', 'bug', 'destroying') but the overall sentiment is positive ('solved').

text: The stock market saw a massive crash today.
rationale: Financial news; testing if 'crash' (usually an app bug) incorrectly triggers negative sentiment.

text: Absolutely perfect if you enjoy wasting your money.
rationale: Starts with 'Absolutely perfect' to trick the model, ending with a negative condition.

text: Fine.
rationale: One word expressing resignation; tests boundary between neutral and negative.

text: I am completely free from the premium subscription trap.
rationale: Contains 'trap' and 'subscription' (often negative) but user is expressing relief ('free').

text: It wasn't as bad as everyone said it would be.
rationale: Uses 'wasn't' and 'bad' but the overall meaning is mildly positive/relieved.

text: The hurricane destroyed the coastal town.
rationale: Objective reporting of a negative event; testing if factual tragedy is misclassified as negative sentiment.

text: Best app ever for testing my patience.
rationale: Uses 'Best app ever' but the object is a negative experience ('testing patience').

text: Why?
rationale: Single question word; tests how the model handles a pure query with no sentiment adjectives.
